title: SelfOp: An Optimization Algorithm for Self-Improving Security Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.22792v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used for security tasks: vulnerability discovery, exploit reproduction, and patch generation. Improving them at the model level demands expert demonstrations or computable rewards, which security tasks rarely offer: traces are costly, failures hard to diagnose, rewards sparse, and non-computable. Efforts thus shift to the harness and context, but manual tuning needs task-specific expertise and scales poorly, while automated methods rely on scarce ground truth, stronger optimizer models, or unguided propose-and-evaluate loops that reduce to costly trial and error.   We introduce SelfOp, an algorithm that automatically improves a frozen security agent's task context (instructions, skills, and reference documents), without modifying its execution harness and model weights. translated_title: SelfOp：一种面向自我改进安全智能体的优化算法
translated_abstract: LLM智能体正越来越多地被用于安全任务：漏洞发现、漏洞利用复现和补丁生成。在模型层面改进它们需要专家演示或可计算的奖励，而安全任务很少能提供这些：轨迹成本高昂、失败难以诊断、奖励稀疏且不可计算。因此，研究努力转向了执行框架和上下文层面，但手动调优需要特定任务的专业知识且难以规模化，而自动化方法则依赖于稀缺的真实标注数据、更强的优化器模型，或无引导的“提出-评估”循环，后者会退化为代价高昂的试错。我们提出了SelfOp，这是一种能够自动改进冻结安全智能体任务上下文（指令、技能和参考文档）的算法，且无需修改其执行框架和模型权重。SelfOp将上下文优化转化为受链式法则启发的文本梯度下降：从单个实例的结果出发，它传播错误信号……
tldr: SelfOp提出了一种受链式法则启发的文本梯度下降算法，通过自动优化冻结安全智能体的任务上下文（而非模型权重或执行框架），在无需专家演示或可计算奖励的情况下实现安全智能体的自我改进。
en_tdlr: SelfOp introduces a chain-rule-inspired textual gradient descent algorithm that automatically optimizes a frozen security agent's task context (rather than model weights or harness), enabling self-improvement without requiring expert demonstrations or computable rewards.
